newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX CRUDE, PRODUCTS TO TREK SLOWLY HIGHER. [CORRECTED 13:22 GMT]
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX CRUDE, PRODUCTS TO TREK SLOWLY HIGHER. [CORRECTED 13:22 GMT]

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* The market is still looking for crude to close above the psychological $20 barrier for the move up to continue.
* Gasoline has improved a little after Tuesday's rally with long term
uptrend support stemming back to June 23's 54.85 cent low coming in at around 62.50 cents today.

NYMEX crude and products futures are expected to continue their trek higher on Wednesday but some analysts see the uptrend for crude breaking down from above $20 unless products can offer fresh impetus.
Gasoline gave the complex a lift on Tuesday, opening near the low but trading bullishly higher over the day to end well above long term trend line support that came in around 62.40 cents a gallon.
Analysts said this was a good sign but some were still looking for confirmation that the current uptrend is not just a correction.
"(NYMEX crude) did not close above $20 and Brent still has a strong resistance above $18.80 to overcome before an extension becomes truly realistic," (corrects quote) GNI said in their daily report.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International was more bearish for the short term market though he saw the bull trend intact for the longer term.

"I am still looking for prices to go under Friday's low from little above current levels. To a bigger degree I still think all the action from June was corrective and eventually it will be fully retraced before the long term bull trend resumes".

After touching off parallel trendline support at $19.68 on Tuesday, crude gapped higher in ACCESS trade on Wednesday with bullish underlying sentiment leaving the market apparently undeterred by a moderately bearish set of API stock data.

This parallel support line comes in at around $18.85 today and is drawn from last Friday's $19.49 low at the same angle and parallel to the bullish trend seen from July 22 to August 5 on the spot month continuation chart.
To the upside a previous support line from July 22 $18.99 low may now provide some resistance but this does not come into play until the around $20.45 analysts said.
On the September chart slow stochastics made a bullish cross at a low level following Tuesday's bullish price action and are now pointing the market higher again.

The picture for gasoline has improved a little after Tuesday's rally. In ACCESS trade the market well above long term uptrend support stemming back to June 23's 54.85 cent low and that comes in today at around 62.50 cents.

However, 10 and 20-day moving average lines are on a path of convergence that could tip the market lower again, though this is countered by Tuesday's bullish stochastics cross on the September chart. RSI's are in neutral territory.
Analysts said heating oil price action is expected to be side ways to higher with the market well supported by double bottom support on the spot chart from Friday and Monday's $54.25 low.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
